Board.tsx renders data-column={status} in both the mobile panel (line 264) and the desktop grid (line 305), so every e2e [data-column="..."] selector matches two elements. Specs work around this with .first() across ~13 files; the workaround relies on (a) mobile-first DOM ordering and (b) Playwright toContainText reading hidden DOM. Triage 2026-04-30 treated each match-failure as a separate test bug rather than fixing the structural duplication. Consider scoping the column marker to a viewport-stable attribute or hoisting the assertion onto a single Board-level element.

authenticate(page, url, slot?) slot param is a silent correctness requirement when two contexts share the same bunker URL — omitting slot causes both contexts to derive the same KP slot from the bunker pubkey, so A2 never appears as a separate leaf; this is not visible from the optional type signature alone
Dead NDKPrivateKeySigner import in src/lib/nostr.ts — imported but never referenced; only NDKNip46Signer is live; a future architect may mistake it for an intentional internal-key-management fixture

EventSignerNdkAdapter constructor does not validate signer arg is truthy — safe today via TypeScript non-nullable type and if(signer) guard at only call site (client.tsx:158), but if adapter's call surface ever widens beyond MarmotProvider the guard should be added: if (!signer) throw new Error('EventSignerNdkAdapter: signer is required')

Multi-user IDB scoping: marmot IDB stores (notestr-groups, notestr-key-packages, notestr-invite-store, notestr-failed-welcomes, etc.) are keyed only by origin, not pubkey. Switching users on same browser leaks prior user's metadata. Spec a per-pubkey partitioning pattern or clear-on-signout policy across the marmot data layer.

vitest node env cannot import .tsx or NEXT_PUBLIC-bearing modules — pure logic must be extracted to .ts sidecar files for unit testability (established pattern: probe-gate.ts, pending-invitations-helpers.ts)

E2E tests cannot use IDB notestr-failed-welcomes count as a pass/fail assertion: the ephemeral relay accumulates Welcome events from prior runs that produce unrelated no_matching_kp records on fresh contexts; sidebar visibility is the correct gate for KP-freshness regressions.
Sibling-forget on same-pubkey siblings silently no-ops after MIP-00 KP change
findings.motivation: AC-E2E-2/AC-E2E-11/AC-E2E-12 are broken for the two-device-same-pubkey flow: a user cannot decommission their other device when both belong to the same Nostr pubkey. This is the same protocol guarantee the self-forget fix (bug-self-forget-no-mls-propagation) just restored, but for the sibling code path.
findings.behavior: Spec e2e/tests/forget-device-sibling.spec.ts:181 hangs the 30s poll: A1 calls sibling-forget on A2 (same pubkey), but A2 leaf stays in A1 ratchet tree (length 2 instead of 1). siblingLeafIndexesForEvents matches relay-fetched KP events to leaves via compareKeyPackageToLeafNode (signaturePublicKey equality). Suspected cause: commit 13297ec (MIP-00 kind-30443 compliance) changed the serialization round-trip such that the decoded relay KP no longer matches the in-tree leaf signature key for siblings. No commit issued; no error surfaced; UI silently does nothing. Same family as the joingroupfromwelcome-throws-no-matching learning.
findings.approach: Two candidates: (1) move sibling-forget to credential-based leaf resolution (mirror self-forget) and disambiguate device-within-pubkey via a new per-slot marker on the leaf (requires protocol amendment because credentials currently carry only the pubkey); (2) repair the KP-shape round-trip drift so compareKeyPackageToLeafNode keeps working — smaller blast radius if a single field-encoding tweak in marmot-ts groups-manager or key-package-event closes it. Investigate (2) first.
findings.success_signal: e2e/tests/forget-device-sibling.spec.ts main test passes (5/5 incl. setup) with A2 leaf gone from A1 view within 30s and A2 slot appearing in __notestrTestForgottenSlots.

findings.text: e2e harness spawns bunkers before port check and leaks serve worker across runs
findings.motivation: 8 manual process reaps were needed across this bug run. Every subsequent e2e run that hits a port conflict will orphan the 3 bunker children already spawned before assertPortFree fires (line 240); serve's npx parent-child split means killing the recorded servePid does not kill the actual HTTP worker, so port 3100 stays occupied across sessions and the next run fails loud before any test runs. Cost of inaction: every e2e run becomes fragile on port collision and requires manual operator cleanup.
findings.behavior: globalSetup spawns bunkerA, bunkerB, bunkerC (lines 197-236) and only then calls assertPortFree(3100) — if the port is busy the three bunker children are already alive and untracked in .state.json. serve is spawned with detached:false but npx forks a child worker; teardown kills serveProc.pid (the npx parent) but not the child serve process, which survives and holds port 3100 into the next session. No process-group kill is used anywhere in teardown.
findings.approach: Move assertPortFree(3100) to before bunker spawns (before line 196). Change serve spawn to detached:true and record process.pid of the serve child directly, or use kill -- -<pgid> in teardown. Write bunker PIDs to .state.json only after all three are live so a setup abort leaves .state.json absent rather than partially written.
findings.success_signal: A deliberate port-3100 collision test leaves zero orphan processes and teardown exits cleanly with no manual intervention.

findings.text: device-store: defaultDeviceName format has no AC
findings.motivation: UI displays either 'this browser' or device-<slot[0..6]>; no epic specifies this contract.
findings.behavior: defaultDeviceName returns 'this browser' iff clientId matches localClientId, else 'device-' followed by the first 6 chars of clientId.

findings.text: device-store: device rename trim + fallback has no AC
findings.motivation: Whitespace in user-typed names is silently trimmed and blank input falls back to the synthetic default — observable but unspecified.
findings.behavior: setDeviceName persists name.trim() if non-empty; otherwise persists defaultDeviceName(clientId).

findings.text: device-store: firstSeen/lastSeen timestamp semantics have no AC
findings.motivation: Device-tracking UI relies on stable firstSeen and monotonic lastSeen; no epic owns this contract.
findings.behavior: markDeviceSeen and setDeviceName set firstSeen on create, preserve it on update, and advance lastSeen to Date.now() on every write.

findings.text: device-store: listDevices null-tolerance and sort order have no AC
findings.motivation: UI list must be stable and tolerant of keys/getItem races; no epic owns the contract.
findings.behavior: listDevices filters out null entries and sorts the remainder by name via localeCompare.

findings.text: device-store: invited-keys clear-by-group prefix contract has no AC
findings.motivation: clearInvitedKeysForGroup uses groupId-prefix matching; sibling-group isolation is observable but unspecified.
findings.behavior: clearInvitedKeysForGroup removes exactly the keys starting with the groupId prefix.

findings.text: device-store: joined-groups trio contract has no AC
findings.motivation: markGroupJoinedFromWelcome / isGroupJoinedFromWelcome / forgetJoinedGroup form the sibling-auto-invite suppression substrate; no AC defines them. AC-CLEANUP-4 mentions the store but not the helpers' semantics.
findings.behavior: mark sets the group as joined-from-welcome; is checks it; forget undoes it; cross-group isolation holds.

archive.text: epic-e2e-relay-state-isolation: per-spec docker compose restart relay auto-fixture to wipe stale kind-30443 KeyPackages between spec files.
archive.reason: Relitigates the 2026-05-01 reversal in commit 7b31ba1. The per-spec _relayReset fixture was tried, broke 'npx playwright test' for callers without the relay container up, and masked test-design bugs behind sweeping cleanups. The standing principle (feedback_e2e_relay_independence.md) is that e2e tests must pass against any relay state via within-test isolation: pinClientSlot, rotated bunker keys, Date.now() group names, clearAppState — not fixture-level resets. If a test seems to need a clean relay, the test has a bug.

archive.text: Including kinds 443, 444, 445, 0, 1059 in NIP-46 perms list because marmot-ts documentation implied they were user-signer kinds
archive.reason: S5 implementation verified via marmot-ts dist/client/group/marmot-group.js and applesauce-common/dist/operations/gift-wrap.js: kind 443 is legacy and query-only; kind 444 is an unsigned NIP-59 rumor by design; kind 445 uses an ephemeral key via finalizeEvent; kind 1059 (gift wrap outer) also uses an ephemeral key; kind 0 is not exercised. The actual user-signer kind for sending MLS welcomes is kind 13 (NIP-59 Seal), which was absent from the original spec list. The spec's architecture context was based on marmot-ts kind numbers, not on which signing path the user signer was actually routed through.
